title: Record the review of phase 4: three findings, fixed
message:
Record the review of phase 4: three findings, fixed

The plan's phase 4 record gains the review of MR !27: the three
findings, the commit that fixes each, what the fix replaces among the
decisions above, the tests, and the verification on f6e48f0e9. Work
item #32 is filed for the body that stat file leaves in room 0.

title: Write the empty save of a leave without a save a second time
message:
Write the empty save of a leave without a save a second time

extract_char_final() tried the empty save once and read nothing back.
When objsave_write_player_save() could not start its transaction,
delete the rows or commit, the last save's rows stayed while the
objects lay in the room, and the next login brought all of them back:
the duplication d989a8517 set out to stop.

The save is now tried once more, as objsave_save_and_extract() does for
the rent, idle and cryo saves; after two failures the staff are told
through mudlog() that the character's next login brings back what it
dropped.

Test_leaving_without_a_save_writes_the_empty_save_again_and_tells_the_staff:
the connection goes as the first attempt deletes the last save's rows,
and the second empties the save with the staff told nothing; then the
database is away for both attempts, the last save stands, and the staff
hear of it. On the commit before, its first half fails with the row
still there.

docs/systems/SAVE_SYSTEMS_BREAKDOWN.md says so.

Review of MR !27, finding 3.

title: Answer NULL for the bags of a character without bag storage
message:
Answer NULL for the bags of a character without bag storage

get_char_bag() read ch->bags without a check. Only init_char(),
new_char() and the login path allocate bag storage: a player body built
for a staff command, as stat file builds one for a player who is not
online, has none, and neither has a mobile. The bag loop
extract_char_final() gained in be819da53 called get_char_bag() for
every player, so such a body ended the server in a segmentation fault
when it was extracted, as empty_bags_to_inventory() would have before.

get_char_bag() now returns NULL when there is no bag storage, which
also covers the loop objsave_save_and_extract() gained in the same
commit. The extraction loop no longer needs its mobile check.

Test_gameplay_extraction_of_a_player_body_without_bags builds a body as
stat file does, puts it in a room and extracts it: the room is as it
was. On the commit before, it ends in SIGSEGV in get_char_bag().

Review of MR !27, finding 2.

title: Refuse put and get into a bag for a character without bags
message:
Refuse put and get into a bag for a character without bags

0980ae2dc's check in do_sort() left sort_object_bag(), which it shares
with do_put() and do_get(), without one: "put <item> bagN" and
"get <item|all> bagN" run by a mobile reached get_char_bag() through it
and ended the server in a segmentation fault. The sort-to path needed
the check for more than the crash: obj_from_char() followed by
obj_to_bag() with no bag storage leaves the object in object_list, held
by no one.

The check moves from do_sort() to the top of sort_object_bag(), so the
three commands share it; every do_sort() path that touches a bag passes
through there.

Test_gameplay_bag_commands_refuse_a_character_without_bags adds put and
both forms of get: eight refusals, and the gem stays carried. On the
commit before, it ends in SIGSEGV at the put.

Review of MR !27, finding 1.

title: Record phase 4 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !27
message:
Record phase 4 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !27

Phase 4's record says what was built for work item #16: why the plan's
check before the change failed and the defect fixed first (a leave
without a save kept the object save of what it dropped), the bag fix
and where it departs from the plan's decisions, the bag-command crash
found on the way, what is left as it is, and the verification.

title: Tell a character with no bag storage that it has no bags
message:
Tell a character with no bag storage that it has no bags

do_sort() (sortto and sortfrom) and do_bags() read the bag storage of
the character that runs them, and a mobile has none: its bags pointer
is NULL, and get_char_bag() and count_bag_contents() dereferenced it.
command_interpreter() lets a mobile run any command below immortal
level, these included, so either command ended the server in a
segmentation fault.

Both commands now tell such a character "You have no bags." and do
nothing else.

Test_gameplay_bag_commands_refuse_a_character_without_bags runs both
sort commands and both forms of bags as a mobile carrying a gem: it is
told five times and keeps the gem. Without either check it ends in
SIGSEGV.

Found while working on work item #16.

title: Take a leaving character's bagged objects along with the rest
message:
Take a leaving character's bagged objects along with the rest

empty_bags_to_inventory() only unlinked each bagged object: nothing put
it in the inventory and nothing extracted it, so it stayed in
object_list, held by no one, after its owner left the game. It also
passed bag number 1 to obj_from_bag() for all ten bags, so the move it
reported named bag 1, and it advanced each bag's list by hand because
obj_from_bag() looked for the object in the wrong one.

- extract_char_final() takes each bagged object out of its own bag and
  puts it in the room, as it does the carried and worn ones, and the
  previous commit keeps the object save from bringing it back. The move
  names the bag. empty_bags_to_inventory(), its one caller gone, goes
  too: a stop in the inventory would report a move from bag to
  inventory, which the quest system counts as finding the object, for a
  character that is leaving.
- objsave_save_and_extract() extracts the bagged objects where it
  extracts the worn and carried ones, after the rent, idle or cryo save
  that wrote them. extract_obj() already takes an object out of its bag.

Test_leaving_saves_keep_the_bags_and_take_them_along replaces
Test_cryo_and_idle_saves_keep_what_is_in_the_bags, which took its
bagged gem out by hand: after a cryo save the bags are empty and
object_list is too, and a load from the saved rows puts each gem back in
its bag, bag 1 and bag 3. The leave without a save in
Test_leaving_without_a_save_drops_everything_and_keeps_no_object_save
now has a gem in bag 1 and one in bag 3: both end in the room, each
moved there from the bag it names.

Work item #16.

title: Keep no object save for what a character dropped as it left
message:
Keep no object save for what a character dropped as it left

extract_char() drops what a character still holds in the room when it
leaves the game without a save: a purge by the staff, a duplicate
removed at login, a quit while free_rent is off. The last object save
still held those objects, so the next login brought them back beside the
room's copies. Crash_delete_crashfile() was meant to prevent that, and
deletes a crash save's file, but under OBJSAVE_DB it returns at once,
and the database rows stayed.

extract_char_final() now writes the character's object save again once
it has dropped anything. The character holds nothing by then, so the
save is empty: the rows, the header and the file all say so. A
character that left with a rent, idle or cryo save holds nothing at
that point, and its save stands. The call to Crash_delete_crashfile()
there goes. Making that function work under OBJSAVE_DB instead would
also delete the crash save at every death, its other two callers, where
the character keeps all its objects.

Test_leaving_without_a_save_drops_everything_and_keeps_no_object_save
crash-saves a carried and a worn gem, extracts the character, and finds
both in the room and no saved row; before the change both rows stayed.

Work item #16.
